objective: I can practice eating a variety of foods. I will do one step at a time and check one result.
scenario: A trusted adult helps the learner look at what foods are already available at a regular meal or snack time, and together they choose four items that are different colors or come from different food groups, arranging them on one plate or in one bowl before eating.
safetyNotes: This task is about trying variety and enjoyment, never about restricting, forcing, or rewarding a food choice.
No food item is labeled as good or bad; the only goal is naming colors and food groups.
If four differently colored items are not available that day, use the simulation alternative instead of pressuring the learner to eat a disliked item.

simulationAlternative.description: If a real plate cannot be built that day, the learner instead plans or draws a variety plate using four foods they already know are typically available in their household, labeling each item's color and food group on the drawing.

materials: learner-local: four food items of different colors or food groups already on hand

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g3-u04-l04-model-card. Watch one complete example.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g3-u04-l04-guided-card. Do the coached move.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g3-u04-l04-independent-card. Choose one complete route. Follow its steps.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g3-u04-l04-evidence-record. Save one result and one reflection.

prompts.text: Describe one of the four items on your plate: its color or food group, and one thing you noticed about it, such as texture, taste, or how it looked.

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g3-u04-l04-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g3-u04-l04-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g3-u04-l04-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Variety achieved: The plate includes four different colors or food groups, confirmed by the guardian. | Naming accuracy: The learner names each item's color and food group out loud before eating. | Engagement without pressure: The learner names and briefly describes all four items in a neutral way, regardless of whether any item is familiar or new. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g3-u04-l04-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner build a second variety plate at a different meal, choosing four food groups different from the first plate, and compare in writing which four groups were picked each time.

resources.title: eating a variety of foods worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: A trusted adult helps the learner look at what foods are already available at a regular meal or snack time, and together they choose four items that are different colors or come from different food groups, arranging them on one plate or in one bowl before eating.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact eating a variety of foods decision or action.
Model move 2: Before looking at what is available, make a guess.
Model move 3: With your adult, look at what is available and choose four items that are different colors or food groups, then name each one out loud before eating.

Model check: Variety achieved: The plate includes four different colors or food groups, confirmed by the guardian. | Naming accuracy: The learner names each item's color and food group out loud before eating. | Engagement without pressure: The learner names and briefly describes all four items in a neutral way, regardless of whether any item is familiar or new.

content: 1. Read the goal for eating a variety of foods.
2. Watch the worked move on swk-rfl-g3-u04-l04-model-card.

resources.title: eating a variety of foods coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: A trusted adult helps the learner look at what foods are already available at a regular meal or snack time, and together they choose four items that are different colors or come from different food groups, arranging them on one plate or in one bowl before eating.
Coach direction: Before looking at what is available, make a guess.
Learner prompt: Guess two food colors you think you will be able to find today, before you look.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: eating a variety of foods complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: With your adult, look at what is available and choose four items that are different colors or food groups, then name each one out loud before eating.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I looked at what foods were already available with my adult before choosing any items.
Response 2 (t2-p2): I chose four items that were different colors or from different food groups, not four of the same type.
Response 3 (t2-p3): I said each item's color and food group out loud before eating it.
Response 4 (t2-p4): If one item was not appealing, I swapped it for a different available color instead of skipping the task.

Equal-access rule: If a real plate cannot be built that day, the learner instead plans or draws a variety plate using four foods they already know are typically available in their household, labeling each item's color and food group on the drawing.

resources.title: eating a variety of foods minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Describe one of the four items on your plate: its color or food group, and one thing you noticed about it, such as texture, taste, or how it looked.

Success checks: Variety achieved: The plate includes four different colors or food groups, confirmed by the guardian. | Naming accuracy: The learner names each item's color and food group out loud before eating. | Engagement without pressure: The learner names and briefly describes all four items in a neutral way, regardless of whether any item is familiar or new.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: eating a variety of foods supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g3-u04-l04-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g3-u04-l04-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional eating a variety of foods condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Variety achieved: The plate includes four different colors or food groups, confirmed by the guardian. | Naming accuracy: The learner names each item's color and food group out loud before eating. | Engagement without pressure: The learner names and briefly describes all four items in a neutral way, regardless of whether any item is familiar or new..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g3-u04-l04-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

guardianInvolvement.role: Give permission; provide only the supervision, handling, review, or observation named in the lesson; attest only that the physical event occurred.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
